A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the posterior parietal lobe (PPC) is involved in processing of temporal information in the human tactile system.
the right PPC plays a more dominant role in this integration process than the left PPC.
the PPC is a key brain region involved in integrating information from different modalities and in the processing of information related to the spatial configuration of the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PPC is involved in the processing of vibrotactile signals that are confounded by arm position in space, and that this processing occurs in a hand position-dependent manner.
the PPC plays a role in integrating tactile information with spatially related proprioceptive information to support the ability to judge which of two stimuli was presented first.
